claim_ceiling: A coverage measurement of the product's own test guard over the committed tree. It is not an audit verdict, scores no frozen bar, reads no Frontier verdict, and asserts nothing about pass/fail.
non_claims: A bare test-count claim (e.g. '924 collected') in a report that cites SEVERAL regression artifacts is NOT attributed to any of them. The report states numbers from its OWN artifact while citing older ones, so the attribution is ambiguous by construction; treating it as a defect would manufacture one.
A single-module pytest run inside a results table ('pytest product/tests/test_x.py - 42 passed') is not a suite count and is deliberately not compared to suite artifacts.
The guard cannot verify that a number is the RIGHT number when no artifact carries it. It verifies agreement with a cited artifact and the internal arithmetic of a decomposition.
A wrong number hidden inside a blockquote or fenced block is not detected here. That is concealment rather than drift, and it is named instead of left implicit.
Which COMMIT produced each part of a collected-test delta is measured by product/test_delta_attribution.py and pinned in product/tests/test_delta_attribution.py, not by this guard.
